result:
I've verified round 276 and my verdict is **PASS**. All browser rows ran in real Chromium at 1440×900 and 1280×720 (Tab order also at 375×812). For comparison I ran a second server at the published code (`a4c0e24`). One half-row fails, and it was already failing there; there are also two Low findings for B.

**What works:**
- The seven unavailable transport buttons can now be reached with Tab: 14 stops instead of 7, in the specified order, and the same set in reverse with Shift+Tab.
- Each one reports as disabled to a screen reader, with its reason as the description.
- Enter, Ctrl+Space and a mouse click on them change nothing.
- After Delete, Undo, Redo or the last Zoom back, focus moves to the partner button as specified.
- The `?` shortcut sheet returns focus to Undo when it closes.
- Space still starts and stops playback when one of these buttons has focus.
- The keyboard shortcuts give exactly the same status messages as before.

**Look:** the greyed label is slightly brighter than before (ΔE about 2.3, the colour difference B predicted, under its limit of 3). The focus ring is as strong as on Fit (5.43:1), the buttons no longer shrink when pressed, and the hover colours of the other buttons are unchanged. No new permanent text was added to the screen.

**Other checks:**
- Only the allowed files changed, and the frozen-file checksum check passes.
- B's code claims match the published code exactly.
- The 20 targeted test files pass (379 tests), and the two required test mutants (M1, M3) both turn red.
- Playback and export still work: the exported WAV is byte-identical to round 275.
- Without sign-in, the demo page opens, the premium page shows "Sign in required" and the audio-token request returns 401.
- Doc 206 and the retro corrections B made (RT-FIX 276) are accurate.

**Findings for B:**
- **C-R276-01 (Low): the hand cursor still shows on unavailable buttons.** The task expected a "not allowed" cursor, but all seven show the pointing hand. Native disabled buttons on the published code do the same. The cause is an unconditional `button { cursor:pointer }` rule on `app/styles/app.css` line 483, which overrides the new utility class. A stopped and asked for a ruling, and B hasn't given one yet. B can either allow edits to that line or use the stronger `aria-disabled:cursor-not-allowed!` class, which stays within this round's allowed files.
- **C-R276-02 (Low): clicking a greyed button no longer saves a half-typed value.** If you type 97 in the tempo field and then click the greyed Undo, the tempo stays unsaved and the cursor stays in the field. On the published code that click saved it. The spec asked for this focus behaviour, and the value still saves on Enter or when the field loses focus. B needs to decide whether this is acceptable.
- **Delete button label (Low, already raised by A's code reviewer):** when nothing is selected, a screen reader announces "Delete — the selected clip; leaves a gap" and then "select a clip … first". The label was frozen by the task, so this isn't A's fault, but it is now reachable with Tab.

The gate script reads only `taskStatus`, so a PASS with one failed half-row will not block publishing. That is intended, because the task sends only Medium or worse look failures back for a fix. The source tree is unchanged, and the temporary copies and the second server are removed.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`; open `c-round-276.md` first.
